sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Package details and command list
sections.what: Describes the database package and lists the commands developers can run, such as generating code, building, migrating, seeding, and resetting the database.
sections.why: Likely reason: one set of named commands keeps database work consistent across the team. Reason for each command is not stated.
sections.watch_out: The db:reset command deletes all data in whichever database the connection setting points to, so it must never point at production.

summary: Defines the database package: its name, its build and database scripts, and the libraries it needs.
purpose: Gives the workspace one set of commands to build, check, and manage the database layer, including the Prisma tool that talks to the database.
why: Likely reason: the database code is shared by other packages, so it is packaged with its own scripts. Reason stated only implicitly.
how: First it names the package and points its main entry to the public index file. Then it lists scripts to generate the database client, build, lint, type check, create and apply migrations, seed starter data, open the Prisma studio viewer, and reset the database. Last it lists the runtime and development libraries.
inputs: A Prisma schema and migration files, which are not in this packet. Commands run from a developer's terminal or a build system.
outputs: Generated database client code, build output, and changes to the database when migrations, seeding, or resets run.
risks: The db:reset script erases the database without a prompt. The db:migrate script is for development and creates new migrations. The db:seed script runs a file that is not in the packet.
debug: If a script fails, run the generate step first because other steps depend on it. Check that the database connection setting is present. For migration problems, compare the migration files with the current database state.
